A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same F-CLIPScore study. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison after matching relocated material.

before.justification: v3 reports original OHD-Caps evaluations, ablations and LLaVA pretraining results on POPE, including appendix experiments.

after.justification: v4 retains those empirical results and adds statistical tests and analyses of training-data filtering.

M1.justification: Noun extraction, sentence/noun score averaging, the training loss and data-filtering procedure remain unchanged. Equation 1 now explicitly includes the image argument, clarifying notation without changing the method.

E1.justification: Both versions use OHD-Caps covering COCO, Flickr30k and NoCaps, LLaVA pretraining data, POPE and Wikipedia nouns for perturbations. The new qualitative analyses examine the existing pretraining dataset.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged, including CECLIP, NegCLIP, the evaluated CLIP-family backbones and the filtering baselines. The CECLIP/NegCLIP comparison moves from v3 Table 5 to v4 Table 4.

E3.justification: Section 4 revises the reported effective LLaVA pretraining batch size from 128 to 256; this does not establish that experiments were rerun. Appendix A adds selection procedures for ten nonoverlapping examples per filter at 30% filtering and the ten examples at each ranking-difference extreme.

E4.justification: New Appendix A compares filter overlap and examines random and extreme-disagreement examples to investigate filtering behavior. Existing noun-replacement and word-type ablations are retained and moved from the appendix into Section 5.1.

E5.justification: Section 3.1 newly reports two-sample t-tests for Figure 2, with p-values of 0.11, 0.67 and approximately zero. The existing ten-run trained-model evaluations and five-seed perturbation uncertainty reporting remain unchanged.

E6.justification: All six retained accuracy tables preserve their numerical entries. New results include filter-overlap rates of 57%, 62%, 67%, 71% and 76%, the t-test outcomes, and qualitative findings concerning text-rendered images and repetitive captions.

T1.justification: The scoring rule and training objective remain mathematically unchanged. Explicit image/caption arguments clarify the existing equations; no new theorem, proof or substantive derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction qualify the vision-encoder argument as applying primarily to discriminative, retrieval-style evaluation. The abstract also specifies that the POPE improvement follows alignment pretraining. The method and data-curation contributions remain.

C2.justification: v4 explicitly acknowledges that free-form caption-generation hallucination was not evaluated. Appendix A adds interpretations of filtering successes and missed repetitive captions, identifying a tradeoff that complicates filtering-rate selection. Existing SFT and multilingual limitations remain.

D1.justification: The documented pretraining batch size changes from 128 to 256. Appendix B newly states that the LLaVA pretraining code uses Apache License 2.0. Existing learning rates, hardware, training times, parser details and code URL are retained.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and bibliography are unchanged after accounting for layout. Both versions position F-CLIPScore as reassessing the vision-encoder explanation associated with Liu et al. (2024c), alongside the same prior methods.

P1.justification: v4 makes localized scope and notation edits, incorporates the former robustness appendix into Section 5.1, and adds a qualitative appendix, publication information and acknowledgments. Most existing prose and the main section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: v4 substantially expands the visual comparison with Figures 4–5, containing forty image-caption examples. It also moves v3 appendix Tables 3–6 into the main results as Tables 2–5 and relocates the POPE table as Table 6. Figures 1–3 are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The clearer evaluation scope reduces overgeneralization, while new t-tests and filtering examples improve evidential transparency without changing the established accuracy results. The benefit is limited by an inconsistency in Appendix A/Figure 5: the stated ascending-rank subtraction conflicts with the interpretation of positive and negative differences.
